records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח נְחֹ֔שֶׁת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אָרְכּ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה רָחְבּ֑וֹ וְעֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת קוֹמָתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And he made an altar of bronze, twenty cubit[s] its length and twenty cubit[s] its breadth, and ten cubits its height.
pieces: He made a bronze altar {{units:about 30 feet|twenty cubits}} long, {{units:about 30 feet|twenty cubits}} wide and {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} high.

L.1: And he made an altar of bronze; its length [was] twenty cubits and its width twenty cubits, and its height ten cubits.

R.1: Solomon made a bronze altar. It was {{units:about 30 feet|twenty cubits}} long, {{units:about 30 feet|twenty cubits}} wide and {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: the bronze altar: not described in 1 Kings 7
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7 lists the bronze work for the temple but does not describe this altar. 1 Kings 8:64 mentions "the bronze altar that was before Yahweh", which was too small for all the offerings at the dedication. Chronicles gives its size here, at the head of the list of furnishings.

decisions.choice: a very large altar for burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The altar of the tabernacle, made by Bezalel, was five cubits square and three high (Exodus 27:1; 2 Chronicles 1:5). This altar was sixteen times as large in area, fitting the much larger temple and its many sacrifices. Its height suggests steps or a ramp up to it, though none is described.

decisions.choice: he made: Solomon, the subject from 3:1
decisions.reason: The subject is Solomon, who "began to build" in 3:1 and is named again in 4:11, 18 and 19. Chronicles tells the whole work as the king's, while naming Huram as the craftsman in 4:11 and 16.

decisions.choice: Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the Hebrew carries over from 3:1 (m3).

decisions.choice: about 30 feet; about 15 feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the size in feet, with the cubits as the alternative. A cubit is about 18 inches.

records.heading: The temple furnishings

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם מוּצָ֑ק עֶ֣שֶׂר בָּֽ֠אַמָּה מִשְּׂפָת֨וֹ אֶל־שְׂפָת֜וֹ עָג֣וֹל׀סָבִ֗יב וְחָמֵ֤שׁ בָּֽאַמָּה֙ קֽוֹמָת֔וֹ וְקָו֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֥ב אֹת֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he made the sea cast, ten by the cubit from its lip to its lip, round all around, and five by the cubit its height, and a line of thirty by the cubit would go around it all around.
pieces: He made the Sea of cast metal. It was round, {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} from brim to brim and {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high, and it took a line of {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} to measure around it.

L.2: And he made the sea of cast [metal], ten cubits from its brim to its brim, round all around, and its height [was] five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits went around it all around.

R.2: He also made a huge round tank of cast bronze called the Sea. It was {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} across from rim to rim and {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high, and it measured {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} around.

decisions.choice: the Sea: as in 1 Kings 7:23
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 7:23 almost word for word. There Hiram is the one who makes it; here the subject carries on from verse 1. The Hebrew here spells "line" in the usual way, without the extra letter of the written text in Kings.

decisions.choice: the sea: a great basin of water
decisions.reason: The great bronze basin was called "the Sea" because of its size. Verse 6 says it was for the priests to wash in. It took the place of the bronze basin of the tabernacle (Exodus 30:17-21).

decisions.choice: ten across and thirty around: measures in round numbers
decisions.reason: A circle ten cubits across measures a little more than thirty-one around. The writer gives round numbers, or the line may have been measured below the brim, which flared outward like a cup (verse 5).

decisions.choice: a huge round tank of cast bronze called the Sea
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Sea was, so that readers do not picture a body of water (m2), as in 1 Kings 7:23.

records.source: וּדְמ֣וּת בְּקָרִים֩ תַּ֨חַת ל֜וֹ סָבִ֤יב׀סָבִיב֙ סוֹבְבִ֣ים אֹת֔וֹ עֶ֚שֶׂר בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה מַקִּיפִ֥ים אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם סָבִ֑יב שְׁנַ֤יִם טוּרִים֙ הַבָּקָ֔ר יְצוּקִ֖ים בְּמֻֽצַקְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And [the] likeness of oxen [was] under it all around all around, going around it, ten by the cubit, encircling the sea all around; two rows the oxen, cast in its casting.
pieces: Under its brim were figures of oxen all around it, ten {{units:to every 18 inches|to a cubit}}, encircling the Sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.

L.3: And [the] likeness of oxen [was] under it, all around, encircling it, ten to a cubit, going around the sea all around; the oxen [were in] two rows, cast when it was cast.

R.3: Below the rim, two rows of figures shaped like oxen ran all the way around the Sea, ten {{units:to every 18 inches|to a cubit}}. They were cast in one piece with the Sea.

decisions.choice: figures of oxen: 1 Kings 7:24 has gourds
decisions.reason: Where this verse has "the likeness of oxen", 1 Kings 7:24 has "gourds", round knobs. In Hebrew the two words look somewhat alike, and one may have been read for the other in copying. It is also possible that the Chronicler understood the ornaments as small ox figures, matching the twelve oxen beneath (verse 4). The Hebrew of Chronicles is followed.

decisions.choice: under it: below its brim, on the outside
decisions.reason: The ornaments ran around the outside of the basin below the rim, as 1 Kings 7:24 says ("under its brim"). They are distinct from the twelve large oxen the Sea stood on (verse 4).

decisions.choice: cast in its casting: made in the same pour as the basin
decisions.reason: The figures were not added afterwards but cast together with the Sea, as in 1 Kings 7:24.

decisions.choice: under its brim; below the rim
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the figures were (m2). Readable puts the two rows first and says "figures shaped like oxen".

records.source: עוֹמֵ֞ד עַל־שְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר בָּקָ֗ר שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה פֹנִ֣ים׀צָפ֡וֹנָה וּשְׁלוֹשָׁה֩ פֹנִ֨ים׀יָ֜מָּה וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה׀פֹּנִ֣ים נֶ֗גְבָּה וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פֹּנִ֣ים מִזְרָ֔חָה וְהַיָּ֥ם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְכָל־אֲחֹרֵיהֶ֖ם בָּֽיְתָה׃
records.gloss: Standing on two [and] ten oxen, three facing northward, and three facing westward, and three facing southward, and three facing eastward; and the sea [was] on them above, and all their hindquarters [were] inward.
pieces: It stood on twelve oxen: three faced north, three west, three south and three east. The Sea was set on top of them, and their hindquarters were all toward the center.

L.4: [It was] standing on twelve oxen, three facing north and three facing west and three facing south and three facing east; and the sea [was] on them, above, and all their hindquarters [were] toward the inside.

R.4: The Sea stood on twelve bronze oxen. Three faced north, three faced west, three faced south and three faced east. The Sea rested on their backs, and their back ends all pointed toward the center.

decisions.choice: as in 1 Kings 7:25
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 7:25 word for word.

decisions.choice: twelve oxen, three toward each direction
decisions.reason: The text gives no meaning for the twelve oxen. The number matches the twelve tribes, which camped three on each side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2), but the writer does not draw that link. King Ahaz later took the Sea down from the oxen (2 Kings 16:17).

decisions.choice: bronze
decisions.reason: Readable says the oxen were bronze (verses 15-16), as in 1 Kings 7:25.

records.source: וְעָבְי֣וֹ טֶ֔פַח וּשְׂפָתוֹ֙ כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שְׂפַת־כּ֔וֹס פֶּ֖רַח שֽׁוֹשַׁנָּ֑ה מַחֲזִ֣יק בַּתִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים יָכִֽיל׃ס
records.gloss: And its thickness [was] a handbreadth, and its lip like [the] work of [the] lip of a cup, a blossom of lily; holding baths, three thousand it would contain.
pieces: It was {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} thick, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could take in and hold {{units:about 18,000 gallons|three thousand baths}}.

L.5: And its thickness [was] a handbreadth, and its brim [was] made like the brim of a cup, [like] a lily blossom; [it was] holding baths: it held three thousand.

R.5: Its walls were {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} thick, and its rim curved outward like the rim of a cup or the petals of a lily. It could hold {{units:about 18,000 gallons|three thousand baths}} of water.

decisions.choice: three thousand baths: 1 Kings 7:26 has two thousand
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:26 says the Sea held two thousand baths. The reason for the difference is not known. It may have come about in copying, since numbers were easily miscopied, or Chronicles may give what the Sea could hold when filled to the brim, while Kings gives its usual load. The Hebrew of Chronicles is followed.

decisions.choice: handbreadth, bath: a hand's width and a measure of liquid
decisions.reason: A handbreadth was the width of four fingers, about 3 inches. The bath was a liquid measure equal to the ephah, perhaps about 6 gallons; its exact size is not known, so the total is an estimate (Ezekiel 45:11).

decisions.choice: holding ... it would contain: two verbs for its capacity
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses two verbs, "holding" and "containing", where Kings has one. Together they stress the full amount it could take.

decisions.choice: about 18,000 gallons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the volume in gallons, with the baths as the alternative; the figure is approximate (m2). Balanced keeps both verbs as "take in and hold"; Readable adds "of water".

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ כִּיּוֹרִים֮ עֲשָׂרָה֒ וַ֠יִּתֵּן חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה מִיָּמִ֜ין וַחֲמִשָּׁ֤ה מִשְּׂמֹאול֙ לְרָחְצָ֣ה בָהֶ֔ם אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הָעוֹלָ֖ה יָדִ֣יחוּ בָ֑ם וְהַיָּ֕ם לְרָחְצָ֥ה לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And he made basins ten, and he put five on [the] right and five on [the] left, to wash in them; the work of the burnt offering they would rinse in them; and the sea [was] for washing for [the] priests in it.
pieces: He also made ten basins for washing and put five on the south side and five on the north. In them they rinsed what was used for the burnt offering, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.

L.6: And he made ten basins, and he put five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them; they would rinse in them the work of the burnt offering; but the sea [was] for the priests to wash in.

R.6: He made ten basins for washing. He put five on the south side and five on the north side. The parts of the animals for the burnt offerings were rinsed in these basins, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.

decisions.choice: the work of the burnt offering: what was prepared for it
decisions.reason: "The work of the burnt offering" means the things made ready for it. The law says the inner parts and legs of the animal were washed before being burned (Leviticus 1:9, 13).

decisions.choice: basins for the offerings, the Sea for the priests
decisions.reason: In the tabernacle one bronze basin served the priests for washing their hands and feet (Exodus 30:17-21). In the temple the work was divided: the ten basins on their stands for rinsing the offerings, and the Sea for the priests. 1 Kings 7:38-39 tells of the basins and their stands but does not give their use.

decisions.choice: right and left: the south and north sides
decisions.reason: The temple faced east, so seen from inside looking out the right is the south and the left the north (verse 10; 1 Kings 7:39).

decisions.choice: a shortened account of the basins and stands
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:27-39 describes at length the ten wheeled stands and their basins. Chronicles names the basins here and the stands only in its list (verse 14).

decisions.choice: south side; north side
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "south" and "north" for right and left (m3), as 1 Kings 7:39 does. Literal keeps "right" and "left".

decisions.choice: the parts of the animals
decisions.reason: Readable says what was rinsed (m1).

records.source: וַ֠יַּעַשׂ אֶת־מְנֹר֧וֹת הַזָּהָ֛ב עֶ֖שֶׂר כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֑ם וַיִּתֵּן֙ בַּֽהֵיכָ֔ל חָמֵ֥שׁ מִיָּמִ֖ין וְחָמֵ֥שׁ מִשְּׂמֹֽאול׃ס
records.gloss: And he made lampstands of the gold, ten, according to their ordinance, and he put [them] in the temple, five on [the] right and five on [the] left.
pieces: He made the ten gold lampstands as they were prescribed and put them in the main hall, five along the south side and five along the north.

L.7: And he made the ten lampstands of gold according to their ordinance, and he put [them] in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.

R.7: He made ten gold lampstands in the way the law said they should be made. He put them in the main room of the temple, five along the south wall and five along the north wall.

decisions.choice: according to their ordinance: made as the law prescribed
decisions.reason: The lampstands were made after the pattern given for the lampstand of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:31-40). The same phrase is used for their lamps in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the temple: the main hall
decisions.reason: The word names the large front room of the house, in front of the inner room, as in 1 Kings 6:3, 17. The lampstands stood there, in front of the inner room (verse 20).

decisions.choice: ten lampstands: in place of the tabernacle's one
decisions.reason: The tabernacle had one golden lampstand with seven lamps (Exodus 25:31-40). Solomon's temple had ten, as 1 Kings 7:49 also says.

decisions.choice: main hall; main room; south side; north
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "main hall" (Readable "main room of the temple") for the large room (m2), as 1 Kings 7:50, and "south" and "north" for right and left (verse 6).

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שֻׁלְחָנוֹת֮ עֲשָׂרָה֒ וַיַּנַּח֙ בַּֽהֵיכָ֔ל חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה מִיָּמִ֖ין וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה מִשְּׂמֹ֑אול וַיַּ֛עַשׂ מִזְרְקֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב מֵאָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he made tables ten, and he placed [them] in [the] temple, five on [the] right and five on [the] left; and he made bowls of gold, a hundred.
pieces: He made ten tables and placed them in the main hall, five along the south side and five along the north. He also made one hundred sprinkling bowls of gold.

L.8: And he made ten tables, and he placed [them] in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. And he made a hundred bowls of gold.

R.8: He made ten tables and put them in the main room of the temple, five along the south wall and five along the north wall. He also made a hundred gold bowls for sprinkling.

decisions.choice: ten tables: 1 Kings 7:48 names one
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:48 names one gold table for the bread of the Presence. Chronicles speaks of ten tables here and of "the tables" for that bread in verse 19 (also 1 Chronicles 28:16). The text does not say whether all ten held the bread or whether some were for other uses.

decisions.choice: bowls: vessels for the blood of the offerings
decisions.reason: These bowls caught the blood of the sacrifices, which was then sprinkled or splashed on the altar (Exodus 24:6; Leviticus 1:5). The word is the one in verses 11 and 22.

decisions.choice: sprinkling bowls; bowls for sprinkling
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the bowls were for (m2), as 1 Kings 7:40 does; "south" and "north" for right and left as in verse 6.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ חֲצַ֣ר הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים וְהָעֲזָרָ֖ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה וּדְלָת֧וֹת לָעֲזָרָ֛ה וְדַלְתוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם צִפָּ֥ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And he made [the] court of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court, and their doors he overlaid [with] bronze.
pieces: He made the court of the priests and the great court, with doors for the court, and he overlaid their doors with bronze.

L.9: And he made the court of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court; and he overlaid their doors [with] bronze.

R.9: He made the courtyard for the priests and the large outer courtyard. He made doors for the outer courtyard and covered them with bronze.

decisions.choice: two courts: an inner court for the priests and a large outer court
decisions.reason: The court of the priests surrounded the temple and held the altar and the Sea; 1 Kings 6:36 calls it "the inner court". The great court lay outside it, where the people gathered (2 Chronicles 6:13; 20:5). 1 Kings 7:12 speaks of "the great court" around the palace and temple buildings.

decisions.choice: court: a second word for an enclosed court
decisions.reason: The verse uses two words for a court. The second, used for the great court, appears in this sense only in Chronicles and Ezekiel (Ezekiel 43:14; 45:19), and also names a ledge of the altar there.

decisions.choice: no parallel in 1 Kings 7
decisions.reason: Kings tells of the courts in 6:36 and 7:12 but not of doors overlaid with bronze. This verse is found only in Chronicles.

decisions.choice: large outer courtyard; outer courtyard
decisions.reason: Readable says the great court was the outer one (m1) and that the doors were for it.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַיָּ֗ם נָתַ֞ן מִכֶּ֧תֶף הַיְמָנִ֛ית קֵ֖דְמָה מִמּ֥וּל נֶֽגְבָּה׃
records.gloss: And the sea he put on [the] shoulder of the right, eastward, from in front of [the] south.
pieces: He put the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner.

L.10: And he put the sea on the right side, eastward, toward the south.

R.10: He put the Sea near the southeast corner of the temple.

decisions.choice: as in 1 Kings 7:39
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:39 gives the same place, with "of the house" after "side".

decisions.choice: the right side: the south
decisions.reason: The temple faced east, so its right side is the south, as the end of the verse makes clear (verse 6).

decisions.choice: south side; southeast corner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "south" for right (m2), as 1 Kings 7:39. Readable adds "of the temple", which Kings has.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חוּרָ֔ם אֶת־הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָק֑וֹתסוַיְכַ֣ל חוּרָ֗ם לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And made Huram the pots and the shovels and the bowls; and finished Huram to do the work which he did for the king Solomon in [the] house of God:
pieces: Huram also made the pots, the shovels and the sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of God:

L.11: And Huram made the pots and the shovels and the bowls. And Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:

R.11: Huram also made pots, shovels and bowls for sprinkling. So he finished the work he did for King Solomon on God's temple. This is what he made:

decisions.choice: as 1 Kings 7:40, with pots, Huram and God
decisions.reason: This verse and the list after it (verses 11-18) repeat 1 Kings 7:40-47. Chronicles has "pots" where Kings has "basins" in this verse; Kings has "pots" in its list (7:45). Chronicles says "the house of God" where Kings says "the house of Yahweh".

decisions.choice: Huram: spelled as read
decisions.reason: The craftsman is called Huram in Chronicles and Hiram in Kings. The second time, the written Hebrew has a different spelling of the name, and the reading tradition gives "Huram" as in the first. It is the same man, the bronze worker of 2:12-13 and 1 Kings 7:13-14.

decisions.choice: pots, shovels and bowls: tools for the altar
decisions.reason: The pots carried away the ashes and the shovels cleared them from the altar (Exodus 27:3). The bowls caught the blood of the sacrifices (verse 8).

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The list of verses 12-16 spells out "the work", so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a colon. Readable adds "This is what he made", as in 1 Kings 7:40.

records.source: עַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם וְהַגֻּלּ֧וֹת וְהַכֹּתָר֛וֹת עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָעַמּוּדִ֖ים שְׁתָּ֑יִם וְהַשְּׂבָכ֣וֹת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְכַסּ֗וֹת אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ גֻּלּ֣וֹת הַכֹּֽתָר֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָֽעַמּוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: pillars two, and the bowls and the capitals on [the] top of the pillars, two; and the networks two, to cover [the] two bowls of the capitals which [were] on [the] top of the pillars;
pieces: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two networks covering the two bowls of the capitals on top of the pillars;

L.12: two pillars, and the bowls and the capitals on top of the pillars, two; and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that [were] on top of the pillars;

R.12: two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; two nets of lattice work to cover those capitals;

decisions.choice: the bowls and the capitals: Kings has "the bowls of the capitals"
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:41 has "the bowls of the capitals"; Chronicles joins the two with "and". The end of the verse here also has "the two bowls of the capitals", so the sense is the same: the rounded parts of the capitals.

decisions.choice: a list running to verse 16
decisions.reason: Verses 12-16 list the bronze work in order: the pillars and their parts, the stands and basins, the Sea and its oxen, and the smaller tools, as 1 Kings 7:41-45.

decisions.choice: those capitals
decisions.reason: Readable shortens the repeated phrase, as in 1 Kings 7:41.

records.source: וְאֶת־הָֽרִמּוֹנִ֛ים אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת לִשְׁתֵּ֣י הַשְּׂבָכ֑וֹת שְׁנַ֨יִם טוּרִ֤ים רִמּוֹנִים֙ לַשְּׂבָכָ֣ה הָאֶחָ֔ת לְכַסּ֗וֹת אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ גֻּלּ֣וֹת הַכֹּֽתָר֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָעַמּוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: and the pomegranates four hundred for [the] two networks, two rows of pomegranates for the network the one, to cover [the] two bowls of the capitals which [were] on [the] face of the pillars;
pieces: the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, in two rows on each network, covering the two bowls of the capitals on top of the pillars;

L.13: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that [were] on the top of the pillars;

R.13: four hundred pomegranates, set in two rows on each net, around the bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;

decisions.choice: as in 1 Kings 7:42
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 7:42 word for word. Each capital had two hundred pomegranates in two rows (3:16; 1 Kings 7:20).

decisions.choice: on the face of the pillars: on top of them
decisions.reason: "Face" here means the surface or top; verse 12 has "on top of" in the same phrase.

decisions.choice: a semicolon at the end
decisions.reason: The list goes on to verse 16, so every level ends the verse with a semicolon, as the parallel does.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַמְּכֹנ֖וֹת עָשָׂ֑ה וְאֶת־הַכִּיֹּר֥וֹת עָשָׂ֖ה עַל־הַמְּכֹנֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And the stands he made, and the basins he made on the stands;
pieces: the stands, with the basins he made for the stands;

L.14: and he made the stands, and he made the basins on the stands;

R.14: the stands, with basins on them;

decisions.choice: the stands: 1 Kings 7:43 has "the ten stands"
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:43 reads "the ten stands, and the ten basins on the stands". Chronicles leaves out the number and twice has "he made". In Hebrew "he made" looks much like "ten", so the words may have been confused in copying. The sense is the same: the ten wheeled stands of 1 Kings 7:27-37 and the ten basins of verse 6.

decisions.choice: the verbs folded into the list
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the list form of verses 12-16 rather than starting new clauses with "he made".

records.source: אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם אֶחָ֑ד וְאֶת־הַבָּקָ֥ר שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֖ר תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: the sea one, and the oxen two [and] ten under it;
pieces: the one Sea, with the twelve oxen under it;

L.15: the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it;

R.15: the one huge tank called the Sea, with the twelve oxen under it;

decisions.choice: the one Sea and its twelve oxen: verses 2-4
decisions.reason: "The one Sea" sets it apart from the ten basins just named. 1 Kings 7:44 has "under the sea" where Chronicles has "under it".

decisions.choice: huge tank called
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader what the Sea was, as in verse 2.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַ֠סִּירוֹת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִ֤ים וְאֶת־הַמִּזְלָגוֹת֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵיהֶ֔ם עָשָׂ֞ה חוּרָ֥ם אָבִ֛יו לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה נְחֹ֖שֶׁת מָרֽוּק׃
records.gloss: and the pots and the shovels and the forks; and all their vessels made Huram his father for the king Solomon [for the] house of Yahweh, bronze polished.
pieces: and the pots, the shovels and the meat forks. All these things that Huram-abi made for King Solomon for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} were of polished bronze.

L.16: and the pots and the shovels and the forks; and all their vessels Huram-abi made for King Solomon [for] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [of] polished bronze.

R.16: and pots, shovels and meat forks. All these things that Huram-abi made for King Solomon for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple were made of polished bronze.

decisions.choice: forks: 1 Kings 7:45 has "bowls"; all their vessels
decisions.reason: Where 1 Kings 7:45 has "bowls", Chronicles has "forks", the three-pronged forks used to take meat from the pot (1 Samuel 2:13-14; Exodus 27:3). The bowls were named in verse 11. Kings has "all these vessels" where Chronicles has "all their vessels".

decisions.choice: Huram his father: the name or title Huram-abi
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Huram his father". As in 2:12, where the king of Tyre calls him "Huram my father", it is taken as part of his name or as a title of honor for a master craftsman, as "father" is used of Joseph in Genesis 45:8. It does not mean that he was Solomon's father.

decisions.choice: polished bronze: burnished to a shine
decisions.reason: The word means rubbed or polished, as in 1 Kings 7:45.

decisions.choice: Huram-abi
decisions.reason: Every level gives the name as one, Huram-abi, as at 2:12 (m2). Balanced and Readable say "meat forks" to show what the forks were for.

records.source: בְּכִכַּ֤ר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ יְצָקָ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בַּעֲבִ֖י הָאֲדָמָ֑ה בֵּ֥ין סֻכּ֖וֹת וּבֵ֥ין צְרֵדָֽתָה׃
records.gloss: In [the] plain of the Jordan cast them the king, in [the] thickness of the ground, between Succoth and between Zeredah.
pieces: The king cast them in the clay ground of the Jordan plain, between Succoth and Zeredah.

L.17: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.

R.17: The king had them cast in molds made in the clay soil of the Jordan Valley, between the towns of Succoth and Zeredah.

decisions.choice: Zeredah: 1 Kings 7:46 has Zarethan
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 7:46, except that it names Zeredah where Kings has Zarethan. The two names are close in Hebrew and probably refer to the same place near the Jordan; a Zeredah in Ephraim is also named in 1 Kings 11:26.

decisions.choice: the thickness of the ground: clay soil used for molds
decisions.reason: The phrase means "thick" or dense ground, that is, clay. The clay of the Jordan valley was suited for making the large molds into which the bronze was poured, as in 1 Kings 7:46.

decisions.choice: the king cast them: the king had them cast
decisions.reason: Huram did the work (verses 11, 16). The king is named as the one who ordered it.

decisions.choice: had them cast in molds; the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable says the king had the work done, that the clay was used for molds (m2), and that Succoth and Zeredah were towns, as in 1 Kings 7:46.

records.source: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֛י לֹ֥א נֶחְקַ֖ר מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת׃פ
records.gloss: And made Solomon all the vessels the these in abundance very, for not was searched out [the] weight of the bronze.
pieces: Solomon made all these things in such great numbers that the weight of the bronze was never found out.

L.18: And Solomon made all these vessels in very great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not found out.

R.18: Solomon made so many of these things that no one ever knew how much all the bronze weighed.

decisions.choice: Solomon made: 1 Kings 7:47 has "Solomon left"
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:47 says that Solomon left the vessels unweighed because there were so many. Chronicles says that Solomon made them in great numbers. Both end with the bronze too much to weigh.

decisions.choice: in abundance very: in very great numbers
decisions.reason: "Abundance" with "very" stresses how great the amount was. Kings doubles "very"; Chronicles has it once.

decisions.choice: the bronze: taken in David's wars
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:8 says David took a great amount of bronze from the cities of Hadadezer, from which Solomon made the Sea, the pillars and the bronze vessels. 1 Chronicles 22:3, 14 say David stored up bronze beyond weighing.

decisions.choice: things
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers tools, vessels and furnishings of every kind. Balanced and Readable say "things" because the list includes pillars and stands, as in 1 Kings 7:45; Literal keeps "vessels".

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְאֵת֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַזָּהָ֔ב וְאֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָנ֔וֹת וַעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לֶ֥חֶם הַפָּנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And made Solomon all the vessels which [were for the] house of God: and the altar of the gold, and the tables, and on them [was] the bread of the Presence;
pieces: Solomon also made all the furnishings of the house of God: the altar of gold; the tables for the bread of the Presence;

L.19: And Solomon made all the furnishings that [were for] the house of God: the altar of gold, and the tables, and on them [was] the bread of the Presence;

R.19: Solomon also made all the furnishings for God's temple: the gold altar for burning incense; the tables for the bread set out before God;

decisions.choice: as 1 Kings 7:48, with "God" and "the tables"
decisions.reason: Verses 19-22 repeat 1 Kings 7:48-50. Here Chronicles says "the house of God" for "the house of Yahweh", and "the tables" where Kings has one table (see verse 8).

decisions.choice: the golden altar: the altar of incense
decisions.reason: The gold-covered altar stood in the main hall in front of the inner room. Incense was burned on it, as on the altar of incense in the tabernacle (Exodus 30:1-10).

decisions.choice: the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set out on the table before Yahweh each Sabbath (Exodus 25:23-30; Leviticus 24:5-9). The name means bread set "before the face" of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: for burning incense; the bread set out before God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the altar was for (m2) and explains "the bread of the Presence" (m3), as in 1 Kings 7:48.

records.heading: The gold furnishings

records.source: וְאֶת־הַמְּנֹר֞וֹת וְנֵרֹתֵיהֶ֗ם לְבַעֲרָ֧ם כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֛ט לִפְנֵ֥י הַדְּבִ֖יר זָהָ֥ב סָגֽוּר׃
records.gloss: and the lampstands and their lamps, to burn them according to the ordinance before the inner room, gold pure;
pieces: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn in front of the inner sanctuary as prescribed;

L.20: and the lampstands and their lamps, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner room, [of] pure gold;

R.20: the lampstands and their lamps, all of pure gold, to burn in front of the inner room as the law said;

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 7:49 gives the places; Chronicles gives the purpose
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:49 says five lampstands stood on the right and five on the left before the inner room. Chronicles gave their places in verse 7 and here says the lamps were to burn "according to the ordinance" (Exodus 27:20-21).

decisions.choice: the inner room: the most holy place
decisions.reason: The word names the innermost room of the temple, where the ark stood (1 Kings 6:16, 19-20).

decisions.choice: pure gold: refined gold
decisions.reason: The word means closed or shut up, and with gold it describes the finest refined gold.

decisions.choice: inner sanctuary; inner room
decisions.reason: Balanced says "inner sanctuary" and Readable "inner room", as in 1 Kings 7:49.

records.source: וְהַפֶּ֧רַח וְהַנֵּר֛וֹת וְהַמֶּלְקַחַ֖יִם זָהָ֑ב ה֖וּא מִכְל֥וֹת זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: and the blossom and the lamps and the tongs [of] gold; it [was] perfection of gold;
pieces: the flowers, the lamps and the tongs of gold, the finest gold;

L.21: and the flowers and the lamps and the tongs [of] gold, it [was] perfection of gold;

R.21: the gold flower decorations, lamps and tongs, made of the finest gold;

decisions.choice: the flowers: blossoms on the lampstands
decisions.reason: The lampstand of the tabernacle had cups shaped like almond blossoms (Exodus 25:31-34). These were flower-shaped parts of the lampstands, as in 1 Kings 7:49.

decisions.choice: perfection of gold: gold of the best quality
decisions.reason: The rare word means completeness or perfection. With gold it describes the purest kind. Kings does not have this phrase.

decisions.choice: flower decorations
decisions.reason: Readable says what the flowers were (m1), as in 1 Kings 7:49.

records.source: וְהַֽמְזַמְּר֧וֹת וְהַמִּזְרָק֛וֹת וְהַכַּפּ֥וֹת וְהַמַּחְתּ֖וֹת זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר וּפֶ֣תַח הַ֠בַּיִת דַּלְתוֹתָ֨יו הַפְּנִימִיּ֜וֹת לְקֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים וְדַלְתֵ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת לַהֵיכָ֖ל זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: and the snuffers and the bowls and the dishes and the firepans, gold pure; and [the] entrance of the house, its doors the inner [ones] to [the] holy of the holies, and [the] doors of the house to the temple, gold.
pieces: the wick trimmers, the sprinkling bowls, the dishes and the firepans of pure gold; and the entrance of the house, its inner doors to the most holy place and the doors of the house to the main hall, of gold.

L.22: and the snuffers and the bowls and the dishes and the firepans, [of] pure gold; and the entrance of the house: its inner doors to the holy of holies and the doors of the house to the hall, [of] gold.

R.22: the wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and fire pans, all of pure gold; and the gold doors at the entrances of the temple: the inner doors to the most holy place and the doors to the main room of the temple.

decisions.choice: the entrance and its doors: 1 Kings 7:50 has the sockets for the doors
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:50 names "the sockets" of the doors, the pivots in which they turned, as gold. Chronicles has "the entrance of the house" and its doors. Kings also lists cups, which Chronicles leaves out here.

decisions.choice: snuffers, dishes, firepans: utensils for the lamps and the incense
decisions.reason: The snuffers trimmed the lamp wicks. The dishes held incense (Numbers 7:14), and the firepans carried burning coals (Leviticus 16:12).

decisions.choice: two sets of doors: the inner room and the main hall
decisions.reason: The doors of the most holy place and those of the main hall are described in 1 Kings 6:31-35. 2 Chronicles 3:14 adds a curtain for the most holy place.

decisions.choice: wick trimmers; the main hall
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "wick trimmers" and "main hall" (Readable "main room"), as in 1 Kings 7:50.
